prompt: Reference images: image 1 shows the chosen GULPER, image 2 shows the chosen DEPTH MINE. Keep each referenced design exactly — silhouette, proportions, colour palette, materials and rendering style — and place them in the new composition described below (framing and background follow the description, not the references): SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen arcade side-scrolling composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. In the lightless deep of a black-blue water trench, the only illumination bioluminescent: a field of tiny glowing specks drifting from dark teal into pale cyan like an inverted star map, rock spires rising in silhouette on both sides, tall weed swaying slow left-to-right across the whole frame. Centered, a GULPER drifts right toward the viewer's ship — a huge-headed deep-sea fish, its mouth a cavernous hinged cage of pale bone ridges taking up half its body, slack-jawed and yawning wide, tiny vicious eyes above the gape, a frayed bioluminescent lure filament dangling from its crown burning pale cyan, its body tapering back into eel-quiet charcoal. Around and below it, a quiet minefield: three DEPTH MINES rest on and hover above the weed — black rounded hulls studded with short contact spikes, each with a single slow-pulsing cyan eye-light, one trailing a loose anchor chain into the dark, one drifting free with a barnacle-crusted flank. From the left edge the MANTA glides in, flat ray-wing pale mint hull dimmed by the depth, green canopy the brightest thing in the water, amber twin thrusters throwing short warm cones that catch the drifting specks — and directly ahead of its path one mine's pulse has just skipped to a faster beat. No explosions yet, pure dread of held pressure. Deep-navy gloom, never pure black. No text, no UI elements. Darks stay a lifted deep navy, never pure black; no letterbox bars, no frame or border around the picture. Every player craft faces right: nose pointing to the right, engines and exhaust on the left. No text, letters, numbers, labels, UI or watermark anywhere.
